name: St. Peter's Basilica
info: St. Peter's Basilica is the church of the Italian Renaissance in Vatican City, begun on 18 April 1506 to replace Constantine's fourth-century basilica and dedicated on 18 November 1626, which Catholic tradition holds stands over the burial site of Saint Peter.

facts.made: Planned by Popes Nicholas V and Julius II; designed principally by Donato Bramante, Michelangelo and Carlo Maderno, with the square and fittings by Gian Lorenzo Bernini; the dome was completed by Giacomo della Porta and Domenico Fontana
facts.form: A cruciform church in the Renaissance style with a Latin-cross nave and a central dome 136.57 metres high and 41.47 metres across inside; an exterior area of 21,095 square metres and an interior area of 15,160 square metres
facts.where: In Vatican City, west of the River Tiber near the Janiculum Hill and Hadrian's Mausoleum, at the head of St. Peter's Square
facts.known: the dome; Michelangelo's Pietà; Bernini's bronze baldachin and Chair of Saint Peter; the tomb that Catholic tradition holds to be Saint Peter's; the papal tombs; Bernini's colonnaded square; the Holy Door opened in jubilee years

t: Pope Julius II decided in 1505 to demolish the fourth-century basilica of Constantine and replace it with a monumental church, and a succession of popes and architects took about 120 years to finish the work.
Bramante, Raphael, Peruzzi, Sangallo, Michelangelo and Maderno each changed the plan, and Michelangelo is regarded as the principal designer of the large part of the building that stands today.

Catholic tradition holds that Saint Peter is buried directly below the high altar, and excavations begun in 1939 found shrines built over an aedicula holding bones, though it could not be determined with certainty that they were Peter's.
dyk: To help pay for the rebuilding, indulgences were granted in return for contributions, and the salesmanship of the preacher Johann Tetzel, appointed by Albrecht of Mainz, provoked a scandal that led to the Protestant Reformation.
ev: Between 319 and 333 the emperor Constantine the Great began the old basilica over the shrine believed to mark Saint Peter's burial place
Pope Julius II decided to demolish the ancient basilica and replace it with a monumental structure
Construction of the present basilica began on 18 April, to the design of Donato Bramante
Michelangelo succeeded Antonio da Sangallo the Younger as superintendent of the building programme
Giacomo della Porta and Domenico Fontana brought the dome to completion
Work began on Carlo Maderno's nave, and the nave was ready for use by Palm Sunday 1615
Pope Urban VIII solemnly dedicated the basilica on 18 November
The Vatican City was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site

sections.origins:
Catholic tradition holds that Saint Peter, chief among Jesus's apostles and the first Bishop of Rome, was martyred in Rome on 13 October 64 during the reign of Nero, after the Great Fire of Rome. The New Testament does not mention his martyrdom in Rome; the tradition rests on the writings of the Fathers of the Church. According to tradition his remains were buried just outside the Circus of Nero, on the Mons Vaticanus, and a shrine was built on the site some years later.

Old St. Peter's Basilica was the church begun by the emperor Constantine the Great between 319 and 333 over the shrine believed to mark Peter's burial place. It had a wide nave with two aisles on each side, an apsidal end and a transept, giving it the shape of a tau cross, and it was over 103.6 metres long. By the end of the 15th century, after neglect during the Avignon Papacy, it had fallen into disrepair. Nicholas V (1447–1455) commissioned work from Leone Battista Alberti and Bernardo Rossellino and ordered the demolition of the Colosseum, so that 2,522 cartloads of stone had been moved for the new building by his death. In 1505 Julius II decided to demolish the ancient basilica altogether, partly to house the enormous tomb Michelangelo was to design for him.
sections.content:
The basilica stands in Vatican City and is approached through St. Peter's Square, a forecourt in two sections, one oval and one trapezoidal, surrounded by tall colonnades. The façade, with a giant order of columns, stretches across the end of the square. The building is cruciform, with an elongated nave in the Latin cross form, but the early designs were for a centrally planned structure and this is still in evidence in the architecture. The dome rises 136.57 metres from the floor to the top of the external cross and measures 41.47 metres across inside.

In the niches of the four great piers under the dome stand colossal statues of Saint Longinus with his spear, Saint Helena with the True Cross, Saint Veronica with her veil and Saint Andrew, whose skull the Vatican possessed until the 20th century; they represent the four major relics believed to be held in the basilica. An entrance hall, the narthex, runs across the building, and one of its bronze doors is the Holy Door, opened only during jubilees. At the heart of the church, beneath the high altar, is the Confessio, an underground chapel at the level of the Constantinian church above the purported burial place of Saint Peter. The interior is decorated with marble, reliefs and gilding, and holds many tombs of popes and other notable people, as well as Michelangelo's Pietà. Its central feature is Bernini's bronze baldachin over the papal altar, and the apse ends in his ensemble containing the Chair of Saint Peter.
sections.making:
A competition was held under Julius II, and Bramante's design was chosen. It was an enormous Greek cross with a dome inspired by the Pantheon, resting on four large piers, and the foundation stone was laid in 1506. After Julius died in 1513, Raphael was confirmed as architect on 1 August 1514 and proposed a nave of five bays. Baldassare Peruzzi reverted to the Greek cross, but Rome was sacked in 1527 and he died in 1536 without his plan being realised. Antonio da Sangallo the Younger then strengthened Bramante's piers, which had begun to crack.

On 1 January 1547 Michelangelo, then in his seventies, became superintendent. He reverted to the Greek cross and redesigned the dome as two brick shells with 16 stone ribs. He died in 1564 leaving the drum complete, and Giacomo della Porta and Domenico Fontana finished the dome in 1590 under Sixtus V. In 1606, under Paul V, the dismantling of the rest of the old basilica began. A committee of ten architects decided in 1607 to extend Michelangelo's building with a nave by Carlo Maderno; work on the nave began on 7 May 1607, with an army of 700 labourers, and Urban VIII dedicated the basilica on 18 November 1626.
sections.reception:
One method used to finance the building was the granting of indulgences in return for contributions. Albrecht, Archbishop of Mainz and Magdeburg, who had debts to the Roman Curia to clear, promoted it and appointed the Dominican preacher Johann Tetzel, whose salesmanship provoked a scandal and led to the Protestant Reformation.

The design drew comment as it changed. When Maderno's nave was planned, the Counter-Reformation increasingly associated a Greek cross plan with paganism and saw the Latin cross as truly symbolic of Christianity. Maderno's façade is often cited as the least satisfactory part of the design; James Lees-Milne finds it too broad for its height, too cramped in its details and too heavy in the attic storey, and the lengthened nave screens the dome from view when the building is approached from the square. Bernini's bell towers were halted in 1642 after cracks appeared, and the idea of completing them was abandoned. The ovoid profile of Michelangelo's dome has been the subject of much scholarship. Lees-Milne cites della Porta as taking full responsibility for the change, while Eneide Mignacca concluded that the profile was part of Michelangelo's first and last concept. Ralph Waldo Emerson called the basilica "an ornament of the earth ... the sublime of the beautiful."
sections.survival:
When the old basilica came down in 1606 the marble cross that Pope Sylvester and Constantine had set on the pediment was lowered, the timbers were salvaged for the roof of the Borghese Palace and two rare black marble columns were stored and later used in the narthex. The tombs of various popes were opened, treasures removed and plans made for re-interment in the new basilica. The central bronze door made by Filarete for the old basilica was enlarged to fit the new narthex, and Maderno's Confessio used marble steps from the old church.

Cracks appeared in the dome in the mid-18th century, and four iron chains were installed between the two shells to bind it; as many as ten chains have been installed at various times. In 1939, under Pius XII, ten years of archaeological research began beneath the crypt, in an area inaccessible since the ninth century. It revealed shrines of different periods built over an aedicula containing bone fragments folded in a cloth with gold decorations and tinted with murex purple. It could not be determined with certainty that the bones were Peter's, but the rare vestments suggested a burial of great importance, and on 23 December 1950 Pius XII announced the discovery of Saint Peter's tomb. In December 2007 a fragment of a red chalk drawing of the dome, almost certainly by Michelangelo, was found in the Vatican archives.
sections.legacy:
The design of the basilica, and in particular its dome, has greatly influenced church architecture in Western Christendom. In Rome, Sant'Andrea della Valle, begun by Giacomo della Porta, was followed by the domes of San Carlo ai Catinari and Sant'Agnese in Agone. Christopher Wren's dome at St Paul's Cathedral in London, Karlskirche in Vienna, St. Nicholas Church in Prague and the Pantheon in Paris all pay homage to it. The architectural revivals of the 19th and early 20th centuries produced many churches that imitate elements of St. Peter's, among them St. Josaphat's Basilica in Milwaukee and Mary, Queen of the World Cathedral in Montreal.

Bernini's square, built between 1656 and 1667, reaches out in two arcs symbolic of the arms of the Catholic Church welcoming its communicants. The basilica is the burial place of 91 popes, along with Queen Christina of Sweden, Countess Matilda of Tuscany and the exiled Stuarts, and Benedict XVI was interred there on 5 January 2023. It is regarded as one of the holiest Catholic shrines. Although it is neither the mother church of the Catholic Church nor the cathedral of Rome, most papal liturgies take place there, and they draw audiences of 15,000 to over 80,000 people.

summary: St. Peter's Basilica, begun in 1506 under Julius II on the site of Constantine's church, was designed by Bramante, Michelangelo and Maderno, with Bernini's square and fittings, and dedicated in 1626. Catholic tradition holds that Saint Peter is buried beneath its high altar.
references: James Lees-Milne, Saint Peter's – the story of Saint Peter's Basilica in Rome (Hamish Hamilton, 1967)
R. A. Scotti, Basilica: The Splendor and the Scandal – Building of St. Peter's (Plume, 2007)
notes: Completion: the lead says construction was completed on 18 November 1626; the Status section says construction finished in 1615 and that Urban VIII dedicated the basilica on 18 November 1626. The text says the nave was ready in 1615 and the basilica dedicated in 1626.

Michelangelo's dome: the article says in one place hemispherical and elsewhere ovoid, and notes Du Perac's engraving may be inaccurate; the text reports only the ovoid-profile scholarship and Lees-Milne/Mignacca views.
